## Shopify vs WooCommerce for an Indian Store: What the Platform Choice Really Costs to Build and Run

For most Indian stores, WooCommerce has the lower monthly platform bill and Shopify has the lower amount of work, and the right choice depends on who will run the store after launch. Shopify charges a monthly plan fee and, because Shopify Payments is not available to Indian merchants, an extra fee on every order paid through an outside payment gateway. WooCommerce is free software, so you pay for hosting, a developer and upkeep instead, with no platform transaction fee. This guide compares the two as a **store-building decision**: what you pay to launch, what you pay each month, where the hidden costs sit, and which questions to settle with your developer before you commit. It replaces an earlier version of this article that focused narrowly on payment fees; the platform decision is wider than that, and so is the cost.

It is written for founders and managers about to build or rebuild an online store, including those speaking to an ecommerce website development company in Pune for the first time. We quote Shopify's published India plan prices as seen on its pricing page when this article was refreshed, and we tell you which numbers will change. We do not quote gateway rates or settlement terms, which vary by provider and negotiation; get current terms in writing from the providers you shortlist.

### The short answer, by situation

| Your situation | Usually leans towards | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Small team, no developer, want to launch fast | Shopify | The platform handles hosting, security patches and checkout; you manage products and orders |
| Content-led brand with a large blog or custom page types | WooCommerce on WordPress | WordPress's publishing tools are strong, and the store lives beside the content |
| Very tight monthly budget but a developer on hand | WooCommerce | No platform subscription or per-order platform fee, if you can manage upkeep |
| Complex custom workflow, B2B pricing, unusual checkout | WooCommerce or a custom build | More control, at the cost of more responsibility |
| Selling mostly cash on delivery | Either; compare carefully | Shopify's outside-gateway fee applies to online payments, not manual methods such as COD |
| Planning heavy growth with a small ops team | Shopify, or a headless approach later | See our guide to [headless commerce for Indian stores](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-headless-commerce-2026) before choosing it |

Treat the table as a starting hypothesis. The rest of this article shows how to test it with your own numbers.

## What Shopify costs in India

Shopify's India pricing page lists these plans. Prices differ by billing period and Shopify revises them, so check the page before budgeting ([Shopify India pricing](https://www.shopify.com/in/pricing)).

| Plan | Per month, billed monthly | Per month, billed annually | Fee when using an outside payment provider |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic | ₹1,994 | ₹1,499 | 2% |
| Grow | ₹7,447 | ₹5,599 | 1% |
| Advanced | ₹30,164 | ₹22,680 | 0.6% |
| Plus | From ₹1,75,000 | Not listed | 0.2% |

Shopify also advertises a short free trial and an introductory low monthly price for the first few months on most plans; the page was showing a 3-day free trial and ₹20 a month for the first three months at the time of writing. Treat promotional terms as temporary.

### The outside-gateway fee, explained plainly

Shopify Payments, Shopify's own payment product, is not offered to merchants in India, so every Indian store uses a third-party gateway. Shopify adds its fee on top of whatever your gateway charges. Payment methods handled manually, such as cash on delivery, are generally exempt from that Shopify fee; confirm this on your plan, since terms can change.

To see the effect, here is a worked illustration using the Basic and Grow percentages above and invented sales figures, for method only. Suppose a store sells ₹4,00,000 a month through an outside gateway.

- On Basic, Shopify's per-order fee is 2% of ₹4,00,000, which is ₹8,000, plus the plan fee of ₹1,499 on annual billing: about ₹9,499 a month to Shopify.
- On Grow, the fee is 1% of ₹4,00,000, which is ₹4,000, plus ₹5,599 on annual billing: about ₹9,599 a month to Shopify.

At that volume the two plans cost almost the same, and above it Grow becomes cheaper; below it Basic does. Your gateway's own charges come on top in both cases and are the same on either plan. The break-even moves with your payment mix, so recompute it with your own sales and with the share of orders that are cash on delivery. Prices and percentages above can change; the method will not.

## What WooCommerce costs in India

WooCommerce is open-source software that runs on WordPress, so there is no licence fee for the core plugin. That does not make it free to run. You pay for:

- **Domain and hosting.** A store needs hosting that can handle checkout traffic reliably. The price range is wide, from basic shared hosting to managed WooCommerce hosting or a cloud server; get written quotes for your expected traffic, because the cheapest plan is often the first thing to fail during a sale.
- **A theme and extensions.** Many themes and extensions have free versions and paid versions with yearly licences. List the extensions you actually need, such as shipping, subscriptions, bookings, invoices and reviews, and add up the licences.
- **Design and development.** The store, its customisation and integrations.
- **Maintenance.** Updates for WordPress, WooCommerce, themes and extensions, security monitoring, backups and fixing conflicts. This is the line that new store owners most often leave out. Our guide on [website maintenance and support](/blog/website-maintenance-support-pune-guide-2026) explains what an ongoing plan should cover.
- **Payment gateway charges,** the same kind you would pay on Shopify, without Shopify's extra fee.

There is no platform transaction fee. The trade-off is that nobody at the platform is responsible for your uptime or security; you, or the company you hire, are.

## Total cost of ownership: the version that decides it

The right comparison is the total over a period such as three years, not the sticker price on day one. Build your own table with these rows and fill it with real quotes.

| Cost line | Shopify | WooCommerce |
|---|---|---|
| One-off: store design and setup | Quote from developer | Quote from developer |
| One-off: migration of products and customers | Quote | Quote |
| Monthly or yearly: platform or hosting | Plan fee | Hosting fee |
| Per order: platform fee on outside-gateway payments | Yes, by plan | None |
| Per order: payment gateway | Provider's rate | Provider's rate |
| Yearly: themes and apps or plugins | App subscriptions | Plugin licences |
| Yearly: maintenance, updates, security, backups | Mostly included in the plan, apart from apps | Developer or agency retainer |
| Yearly: custom development as you grow | Quote | Quote |
| Cost of downtime or a slow store | Lower platform risk | Depends on hosting and upkeep |
| Cost of leaving later | Export and rebuild | Export and rebuild, though you own the code and data |

A common mistake is to compare Shopify's monthly fee with WooCommerce's hosting fee and stop. Apps on Shopify and plugins on WooCommerce often cost more than either, and a developer's time for updates and fixes is a real, recurring cost on WooCommerce.

## Apps and plugins: where the bill creeps

Both platforms are extended with add-ons, and the add-ons decide the final cost.

- **Shopify apps** are usually paid monthly. Several small subscriptions for reviews, upsells, COD verification, WhatsApp messages, wishlists and shipping can add up. Each app also adds code to your pages, which can slow the store; our guide on [why Shopify or WooCommerce stores are slow](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-store-speed-core-web-vitals-2026) explains how to audit this.
- **WooCommerce plugins** are often a yearly licence. They also need updating and sometimes conflict with each other, which is where the maintenance cost comes from.

Before you decide, list every feature you need on day one and in year one, and ask your developer to name the app or plugin for each and its price. Then ask which features they would build custom instead.

## Features that differ in practice

Rather than a long feature matrix, here are the differences that affect most Indian stores.

### Checkout and payments

Both platforms support the common Indian gateways through apps or plugins. Shopify's checkout is hosted by Shopify, which makes it consistent and well-tested but limits how far you can change it; WooCommerce's checkout is yours to customise, which is useful for custom fields and awkward when a customisation breaks. Our guide on [designing a checkout form and guest checkout](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-checkout-form-guest-checkout-2026) covers what the form should do on either platform, and our [payment gateway](/services/payment-gateway) and [checkout system](/services/checkout-system) service pages describe how we integrate them.

### Cash on delivery, pin codes and shipping

Indian stores need COD handling, pin code checks and courier integration. Both platforms rely on apps or plugins for these. Settle which tools you will use, and who verifies COD orders, before development starts. See also our [logistics integration](/services/logistic-integration) page.

### Search engine visibility

Both can rank well when built properly. WooCommerce on WordPress offers fine control over URLs, templates and structured data; Shopify has fixed URL patterns (for example, products live under /products/ and collections under /collections/) that are fine for most stores but less flexible. What decides rankings is mostly the content and structure you build, not the platform. Our guides on [product schema](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-product-schema-shopify-woocommerce-2026), [collection page content](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-collection-page-seo-content-2026) and [faceted navigation](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-faceted-navigation-seo-2026) apply to both.

### Languages

If you need Hindi or Marathi storefronts, check the translation approach for each platform, the SEO treatment of translated pages and the cost of apps or plugins; our article on [multilingual Marathi and Hindi stores](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-multilingual-marathi-hindi-store-2026) goes through the build.

### Invoices and tax documents

Both need configuration or add-ons for GST-compliant invoices. We keep this article to the platform decision; our guides on [GST invoices in WooCommerce](/blog/gst-invoices-woocommerce-india) and [GST invoicing on Shopify](/blog/gst-invoicing-shopify-india) cover the store-build side, and your accountant should confirm the tax treatment.

### Speed and reliability

Shopify's hosting is managed, so the baseline is consistent. WooCommerce performance depends on hosting, caching, theme quality and how many plugins you load. A well-built WooCommerce store can be fast; a neglected one often is not. Ask any developer to show load speed results on a mid-range phone for a store they built, not only a desktop score.

### Control and ownership

With WooCommerce you own the code and the database and can move host. With Shopify you own your content and customer data and can export them, but the platform itself stays with Shopify and you accept its terms and any price changes. Neither is wrong; decide how much that matters to you. Our guide on [what you should own after launch](/blog/web-development-company-pune-website-handover-ownership-checklist-2026) applies to both.

## Hidden costs that change the decision

1. **Developer dependence.** WooCommerce customisations need someone who understands them. If your developer disappears, can another take over? Ask for documentation.
2. **Plan upgrades.** Shopify features and lower per-order fees sit on higher plans. Model what happens when you grow.
3. **App churn.** Apps are discontinued or change prices; plugins stop being updated. Keep the number small.
4. **Migration later.** Moving from one platform to the other is possible, but takes time and care with URLs and redirects. Our guide on [planning website structure and redirects](/blog/web-development-company-pune-website-structure-sitemap-planning-2026) explains why URLs matter.
5. **Security incidents.** On WooCommerce, you carry the patching duty; on Shopify, mostly the platform does. Budget time or money for that duty.
6. **Marketing integrations.** Check tracking, Merchant Center feeds and ad pixels for each platform. Our article on [Google Merchant Center for Indian stores](/blog/ecommerce-website-development-pune-google-merchant-center-2026) covers feed requirements.

## A way to decide in an afternoon

1. **List your must-have features,** on day one and in year one.
2. **Decide who runs the store.** If it is you or a small team with no technical person, weigh managed hosting heavily.
3. **Estimate monthly online sales** and the share paid through an outside gateway versus COD.
4. **Get two quotes for each platform,** including build, apps or plugins, hosting and a maintenance plan.
5. **Build the three-year table above** and compare totals, not line items.
6. **Ask what happens when it breaks,** and who answers the phone.
7. **Decide on reversibility.** Which choice would you find easier to leave?

If the totals are close, choose the platform your team can operate with the least friction; the cheaper platform is not cheaper if it sits half-managed.

## Questions to ask a developer before you commit

1. Which platform do you recommend for us and why, in terms of our team and our numbers?
2. Which apps or plugins do we need, and what will each cost every year?
3. What does ongoing maintenance include, and what is charged separately?
4. How will the store perform on a mid-range phone, and how will we test it?
5. Who owns the store, code, hosting and accounts?
6. What will it take to move to the other platform in future?
7. How are COD, pin codes, invoices and shipping handled?
8. What is the plan for backups and recovery?

Our article on [questions to ask a web development company before requesting a quote](/blog/web-development-company-pune-shortlist-questions-2026) has a longer list for any project.

## Where to start with a store build

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is WooCommerce cheaper than Shopify in India?

Often on the monthly platform bill, because WooCommerce has no subscription or per-order platform fee. But you pay for hosting, plugins and maintenance. Compare the total cost over three years with real quotes, not only the sticker prices.

### Does Shopify charge an extra fee for payment gateways in India?

Yes. Shopify Payments is not available to Indian merchants, so stores use an outside gateway and Shopify adds a fee by plan: 2% on Basic, 1% on Grow and 0.6% on Advanced at the time of writing. Check Shopify's India pricing page for current rates.

### Which platform is better for a small Indian D2C brand?

Shopify suits teams that want a managed platform and a quick launch. WooCommerce suits brands with a developer, content-heavy plans or a need for custom workflows. Choose by who will run the store, not only by price.

### Can I switch from Shopify to WooCommerce later, or the other way?

Yes, but it needs planning: products, customers, orders, URLs and redirects must be moved carefully to protect search rankings and customer records. Keep your product data clean and exportable from day one.

### How much does a Shopify or WooCommerce store cost to build in Pune?

It depends on design, number of products, integrations and custom features, so there is no single figure. Ask for a written quotation that separates build, apps or plugins, hosting and maintenance, and compare at least two.
